literal: The wealth of he who is not desired is like a poisonous tree having ripened inside the middle of the village.
translation: The wealth of a person who is not loved by anyone is like a poisonous tree bearing ripe fruit in the very middle of a village.
modern: பிறரால் விரும்பப்படாதவனுடைய செல்வம், ஊரின் நடுவே நச்சு மரம் பழுத்து நிற்பதைப் போன்றது.
explanation: This couplet compares the wealth of an unloved or miserly person to a poisonous tree bearing ripe fruit in the center of a village. Although the tree is full of fruit and highly visible to everyone, no one can eat it because it is toxic. Similarly, the wealth of a person who does not share or who is disliked by the community is useless to those around him. The key words 'நச்சப் படாதவன்' (he who is not desired or loved) and 'நச்சு மரம்' (poisonous tree) draw a sharp contrast between abundance and uselessness. The image of the tree in the 'நடுவூருள்' (middle of the village) emphasizes that the wealth is in plain sight but remains entirely out of reach for any beneficial purpose.
